output.argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy while the health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed. It does support a narrower certification position: aggregate readiness passed by 2.4 points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and monitoring plus rollback make the launch monitored and reversible. Under the stated policy, that is supportable only if certification is framed on a disclosure basis for the known limitation rather than as if rollout controls cured the weakness. The audit concern should therefore be narrowed from 'noncompliant certification' to 'certification is only supportable as caveated compliance if the packet ties approval to explicit disclosure of the exposed limitation for the named use case.'
output.claims_about_business_cost: Escalating this as if the entire certification request lacks any support would overstate the gap relative to the admissible record. The record shows meaningful readiness and reversible deployment controls, so the remaining issue is how certification is framed and documented, not whether any launch support exists at all. A caveated treatment preserves audit accuracy while avoiding unnecessary delay from treating a bounded documentation and disclosure issue as a total bar on monitored launch.
